title: Prosody-Aware Speech Representations for Emotion Recognition under Pragmatic Ambiguity
abstract: Speech emotion recognition (SER) systems often rely on semantic or spectral representations learned by speech encoders, while prosodic cues conveying emotional intent are not explicitly modeled. In real-world conversations, emotional meaning is conveyed through prosody when linguistic cues alone are insufficient, especially in pragmatically ambiguous utterances. We propose a prosody-aware speech representation for emotion recognition and downstream applications by injecting pitch and energy into shared hidden representations of a pretrained Whisper encoder. We evaluate the approach using a 59-class emotion classification task and a Pragmatic Ambiguity Resolution (PAR) evaluation task. Experiments show improvements up to 13.93%p in emotion classification and 11.6%p in PAR compared to the same Whisper model without prosody. The proposed model also outperforms text-based LLM inference (GPT-4o mini) on PAR, highlighting the importance of prosody-aware representations for emotion systems.
relevance_note: Prosody-aware speech representations for emotion recognition; SER, no synthesis.
